title: ARKST Single-S-Box Spanning Conjecture
summary: ARKST builds a candidate space from differences activating one S-box at a time; whether their span contains every alpha-admissible key difference remains conjectural.

formal_statement.body: For an SPN, ARKST restricts each round's key-difference component $W_i$ to a difference $a_i$ that activates at most one S-box, represented as $a_i=L(c_i)$ with $\operatorname{wt}_b(c_i)\le 1$, and forms a candidate $\alpha$-admissible key-difference space from the linear combinations of the differences obtained in this way. The unresolved question is whether these single-S-box-activation differences span every $\alpha$-admissible key difference, so that the restriction is complete after taking linear combinations, even though individual $\alpha$-admissible differences may activate more than one S-box.

scope.domain: Integral cryptanalysis of SPNs via ARKST's alpha-admissible key-difference search.
parameters: Wᵢ and i: the key-difference component and its round index
aᵢ: a searched difference restricted to activate at most one S-box
cᵢ, L, and b: the representation vector, mapping, and word size used in the block-weight condition
alpha: the admissibility label for the target key-difference space
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether differences activating at most one S-box span every alpha-admissible key difference after taking linear combinations.

citations.label: When the Wrong Key Lives On: The Key-Recovery Procedure in Integral Attacks

progress.summary: The source explicitly conjectures that differences found by activating one S-box at a time span all alpha-admissible key differences. It notes that individual admissible differences need not have this minimal form; the claim concerns their linear combinations.
citation_labels: Christof Beierle et al., When the Wrong Key Lives On: The Key-Recovery Procedure in Integral Attacks
